1 | # Dialect Development - AI Assistant Instructions
2 | 
3 | This file provides guidance for developing and extending SQL dialect support in SQLFluff.
4 | 
5 | ## Overview
6 | 
7 | SQLFluff supports 25+ SQL dialects through an inheritance-based system. Each dialect extends the ANSI base dialect and overrides specific grammar segments to match the target SQL variant's syntax.
8 | 
9 | ## Dialect Architecture
10 | 
11 | ### Inheritance Hierarchy
12 | 
13 | ```
14 | ANSI (base) ← All dialects inherit from here
15 | ├── T-SQL (Microsoft SQL Server)
16 | ├── PostgreSQL
17 | │   └── Redshift (extends PostgreSQL)
18 | ├── MySQL
19 | │   └── MariaDB (extends MySQL)
20 | ├── BigQuery
21 | ├── Snowflake
22 | └── ... (20+ more dialects)
23 | ```
24 | 
25 | ### File Organization
26 | 
27 | ```
28 | src/sqlfluff/dialects/
29 | ├── dialect_ansi.py              # Base ANSI SQL dialect
30 | ├── dialect_tsql.py              # T-SQL (SQL Server)
31 | ├── dialect_postgres.py          # PostgreSQL
32 | ├── dialect_bigquery.py          # Google BigQuery
33 | ├── dialect_snowflake.py         # Snowflake
34 | ├── ...
35 | ├── dialect_ansi_keywords.py     # ANSI reserved/unreserved keywords
36 | ├── dialect_tsql_keywords.py     # T-SQL keywords
37 | └── dialect_instructions/    # Per-dialect agent instructions (optional)
38 |     ├── tsql.md
39 |     ├── postgres.md
40 |     └── ...
41 | ```
42 | 
43 | ## Creating/Extending a Dialect
44 | 
45 | ### Basic Dialect Structure
46 | 
47 | ```python
48 | """The T-SQL (Microsoft SQL Server) dialect."""
49 | 
50 | from sqlfluff.core.dialects import load_raw_dialect
51 | from sqlfluff.core.parser import BaseSegment
52 | from sqlfluff.core.parser.grammar import (
53 |     Sequence, OneOf, Ref, Bracketed, Delimited, AnyNumberOf, Optional
54 | )
55 | 
56 | # Load parent dialect
57 | ansi_dialect = load_raw_dialect("ansi")
58 | 
59 | # Create new dialect as copy
60 | tsql_dialect = ansi_dialect.copy_as("tsql")
61 | 
62 | # Set keywords from separate file
63 | tsql_dialect.sets("reserved_keywords").update([
64 |     "CLUSTERED", "NONCLUSTERED", "ROWGUIDCOL", "TOP"
65 | ])
66 | 
67 | # Define new segments specific to T-SQL
68 | class TopClauseSegment(BaseSegment):
69 |     """TOP clause for T-SQL SELECT statements."""
70 | 
71 |     type = "top_clause"
72 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
73 |         "TOP",
74 |         OneOf(
75 |             Ref("NumericLiteralSegment"),
76 |             Bracketed(Ref("ExpressionSegment")),
77 |         ),
78 |         Sequence("PERCENT", optional=True),
79 |         Sequence("WITH", "TIES", optional=True),
80 |     )
81 | 
82 | # Override existing ANSI segments
83 | tsql_dialect.replace(
84 |     SelectStatementSegment=Sequence(
85 |         "SELECT",
86 |         Ref("TopClauseSegment", optional=True),  # T-SQL addition
87 |         Ref("SelectClauseSegment"),
88 |         Ref("FromClauseSegment", optional=True),
89 |         Ref("WhereClauseSegment", optional=True),
90 |     ),
91 | )
92 | ```
93 | 
94 | ### Grammar Composition Primitives
95 | 
96 | Located in `src/sqlfluff/core/parser/grammar/`:
97 | 
98 | | Primitive | Purpose | Example |
99 | |-----------|---------|---------|
100 | | `Sequence()` | Ordered sequence of elements | `Sequence("SELECT", Ref("SelectClauseSegment"))` |
101 | | `OneOf()` | Choice between alternatives | `OneOf("ASC", "DESC")` |
102 | | `Delimited()` | Comma-separated list | `Delimited(Ref("ColumnReferenceSegment"))` |
103 | | `AnyNumberOf()` | Zero or more repetitions | `AnyNumberOf(Ref("WhereClauseSegment"))` |
104 | | `Bracketed()` | Content in parentheses | `Bracketed(Ref("ExpressionSegment"))` |
105 | | `Ref()` | Reference to another segment | `Ref("TableReferenceSegment")` |
106 | | `Optional()` | Optional element (or use `optional=True`) | `Optional(Ref("WhereClause"))` |
107 | 
108 | When a dialect needs dedicated spacing for `alias(columns)`, give its bracketed
109 | column alias list a segment type such as `alias_column_list`. This avoids relaxing
110 | spacing throughout every `alias_expression`.
111 | 
112 | ### Grammar Organization Patterns
113 | 
114 | #### Internal Grammar (Private Attributes with `_` prefix)
115 | 
116 | Use for grammar components specific to one statement:
117 | 
118 | ```python
119 | class CreateDatabaseStatementSegment(BaseSegment):
120 |     """A CREATE DATABASE statement."""
121 | 
122 |     # Internal grammar - only used in this segment
123 |     _filestream_option = OneOf(
124 |         Sequence("NON_TRANSACTED_ACCESS", Ref("EqualsSegment"), "OFF"),
125 |         Sequence("DIRECTORY_NAME", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("QuotedLiteralSegment")),
126 |     )
127 | 
128 |     _create_database_option = OneOf(
129 |         Sequence("FILESTREAM", Bracketed(Delimited(_filestream_option))),
130 |         Sequence("DEFAULT_LANGUAGE", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("LanguageNameSegment")),
131 |         Sequence("DEFAULT_FULLTEXT_LANGUAGE", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("LanguageNameSegment")),
132 |     )
133 | 
134 |     type = "create_database_statement"
135 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
136 |         "CREATE", "DATABASE",
137 |         Ref("DatabaseReferenceSegment"),
138 |         Sequence("WITH", Delimited(_create_database_option), optional=True),
139 |     )
140 | ```
141 | 
142 | #### Shared Segments (Named Classes)
143 | 
144 | Create separate segment classes for reusable components:
145 | 
146 | ```python
147 | class FileSpecSegment(BaseSegment):
148 |     """File specification - reusable in CREATE/ALTER statements."""
149 | 
150 |     type = "file_spec"
151 |     match_grammar = Bracketed(
152 |         Sequence(
153 |             Sequence("NAME", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("QuotedLiteralSegment"), optional=True),
154 |             Sequence("FILENAME", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("QuotedLiteralSegment")),
155 |             Sequence("SIZE", Ref("EqualsSegment"), Ref("FileSizeSegment"), optional=True),
156 |         )
157 |     )
158 | 
159 | # Now FileSpecSegment can be used in multiple statements
160 | class CreateDatabaseStatementSegment(BaseSegment):
161 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
162 |         "CREATE", "DATABASE",
163 |         Ref("DatabaseReferenceSegment"),
164 |         Sequence("ON", Delimited(Ref("FileSpecSegment")), optional=True),
165 |     )
166 | 
167 | class AlterDatabaseStatementSegment(BaseSegment):
168 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
169 |         "ALTER", "DATABASE",
170 |         Ref("DatabaseReferenceSegment"),
171 |         "ADD", "FILE", Ref("FileSpecSegment"),
172 |     )
173 | ```
174 | 
175 | **Decision criteria:**
176 | - **Use `_prefix` internal grammar** when:
177 |   - Grammar is specific to one statement type
178 |   - No other segments need to reference it
179 |   - Breaking down complex `match_grammar` for readability
180 | 
181 | - **Use shared segment classes** when:
182 |   - Multiple statements use the same construct
183 |   - Construct represents a meaningful SQL element
184 |   - Other rules or segments need to `Ref()` it by name
185 |   - Semantic meaning beyond one statement
186 | 
187 | ## Development Workflow
188 | 
189 | ### Step 1: Create Test SQL Files
190 | 
191 | ```bash
192 | # Add SQL test cases to test/fixtures/dialects/<dialect>/
193 | echo "SELECT TOP 10 * FROM users;" > test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/top_clause.sql
194 | echo "CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX idx_id ON users(id);" > test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/create_index.sql
195 | ```
196 | 
197 | **Test file conventions:**
198 | - Organize by segment type (e.g., `select_statement.sql`, `create_table.sql`, `merge_statement.sql`)
199 | - Include multiple test cases per file covering edge cases
200 | - Use descriptive filenames matching the segment being tested
201 | - Test various keyword combinations, identifier formats, literal types, comments
202 | 
203 | **Example structure:**
204 | ```
205 | test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/
206 | ├── select_top.sql           # TOP clause variations
207 | ├── create_index.sql         # CLUSTERED/NONCLUSTERED indexes
208 | ├── merge_statement.sql      # MERGE operations
209 | ├── pivot_unpivot.sql        # PIVOT/UNPIVOT queries
210 | └── table_hints.sql          # WITH (NOLOCK) etc.
211 | ```
212 | 
213 | ### Step 2: Generate Expected Parse Trees
214 | 
215 | ```bash
216 | # Activate virtual environment
217 | source .venv/bin/activate
218 | 
219 | # Generate YAML fixtures for specific dialect
220 | python test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py -d tsql
221 | 
222 | # Or use tox
223 | tox -e generate-fixture-yml -- -d tsql
224 | ```
225 | 
226 | This creates `.yml` files showing the current parse tree. Initially these may show parsing failures or incorrect structures.
227 | 
228 | ### Step 3: Implement Grammar
229 | 
230 | Edit `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_<name>.py`:
231 | 
232 | ```python
233 | # 1. Define new segments needed
234 | class TopClauseSegment(BaseSegment):
235 |     """TOP clause for T-SQL."""
236 |     type = "top_clause"
237 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
238 |         "TOP",
239 |         Ref("NumericLiteralSegment"),
240 |         Sequence("PERCENT", optional=True),
241 |     )
242 | 
243 | # 2. Override parent segments
244 | tsql_dialect.replace(
245 |     SelectStatementSegment=Sequence(
246 |         "SELECT",
247 |         Ref("TopClauseSegment", optional=True),
248 |         Ref("SelectClauseSegment"),
249 |         # ... rest of SELECT grammar
250 |     ),
251 | )
252 | ```
253 | 
254 | ### Step 4: Regenerate and Verify
255 | 
256 | ```bash
257 | # Regenerate YAML to see updated parse tree
258 | python test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py -d tsql
259 | 
260 | # Check that parsing now works correctly
261 | sqlfluff parse test/fixtures/dialects/tsql/top_clause.sql --dialect tsql
262 | ```
263 | 
264 | > **Propagate grammar changes to the Rust parser.** Dialect grammars are also
265 | > compiled into the Rust implementation (`sqlfluffrs/`). With
266 | > `core.use_rust_parser = auto` (the default when `sqlfluff[rs]` is installed)
267 | > the Rust parser is what actually runs, so a stale Rust build will parse with
268 | > the *old* grammar. Regenerate the Rust dialect tables after editing a grammar:
269 | >
270 | > ```bash
271 | > python utils/rustify.py build   # regenerate; or just rebuild the extension
272 | > ```
273 | >
274 | > A `cargo build` / `maturin develop` also regenerates automatically (see
275 | > `sqlfluffrs/AGENTS.md` → "Syncing with Python").
276 | 
277 | ### Step 5: Run Full Test Suite
278 | 
279 | ```bash
280 | # Test just the dialect
281 | tox -e generate-fixture-yml -- -d tsql
282 | 
283 | # Run full test suite to ensure no regressions
284 | tox -e py312
285 | ```
286 | 
287 | ## Keywords Management
288 | 
289 | ### Keyword Files
290 | 
291 | Each dialect should have a keywords file: `dialect_<name>_keywords.py`
292 | 
293 | ```python
294 | """T-SQL reserved and unreserved keywords."""
295 | 
296 | RESERVED_KEYWORDS = [
297 |     "ADD", "ALL", "ALTER", "AND", "ANY", "AS", "ASC",
298 |     "CLUSTERED", "NONCLUSTERED", "TOP", "PIVOT", "UNPIVOT",
299 |     # ... full list
300 | ]
301 | 
302 | UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS = [
303 |     "ABSOLUTE", "ACTION", "ADA", "ALIAS", "ALLOCATE",
304 |     # ... full list
305 | ]
306 | ```
307 | 
308 | In dialect file:
309 | ```python
310 | from sqlfluff.dialects.dialect_tsql_keywords import (
311 |     RESERVED_KEYWORDS, UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS
312 | )
313 | 
314 | tsql_dialect.sets("reserved_keywords").update(RESERVED_KEYWORDS)
315 | tsql_dialect.sets("unreserved_keywords").update(UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS)
316 | ```
317 | 
318 | ## Common Dialect Patterns
319 | 
320 | ### Adding Vendor-Specific Functions
321 | 
322 | ```python
323 | class TSQLFunctionNameSegment(BaseSegment):
324 |     """T-SQL specific function names."""
325 | 
326 |     type = "function_name"
327 |     match_grammar = OneOf(
328 |         "GETDATE", "NEWID", "SCOPE_IDENTITY",
329 |         "IDENT_CURRENT", "ROWCOUNT_BIG",
330 |         # Add more T-SQL functions
331 |     )
332 | 
333 | tsql_dialect.replace(
334 |     FunctionNameSegment=OneOf(
335 |         Ref("AnsiSQLFunctionNameSegment"),  # Inherit ANSI functions
336 |         Ref("TSQLFunctionNameSegment"),      # Add T-SQL specific
337 |     ),
338 | )
339 | ```
340 | 
341 | ### Adding Statement Types
342 | 
343 | ```python
344 | class MergeStatementSegment(BaseSegment):
345 |     """MERGE statement (T-SQL, Oracle, etc.)."""
346 | 
347 |     type = "merge_statement"
348 |     match_grammar = Sequence(
349 |         "MERGE",
350 |         Sequence("TOP", Ref("ExpressionSegment"), optional=True),
351 |         "INTO", Ref("TableReferenceSegment"),
352 |         "USING", Ref("TableReferenceSegment"),
353 |         "ON", Ref("ExpressionSegment"),
354 |         AnyNumberOf(
355 |             Sequence("WHEN", "MATCHED", "THEN", Ref("MergeActionSegment")),
356 |             Sequence("WHEN", "NOT", "MATCHED", "THEN", Ref("MergeActionSegment")),
357 |         ),
358 |     )
359 | 
360 | # Add to statement grammar
361 | tsql_dialect.replace(
362 |     StatementSegment=OneOf(
363 |         Ref("SelectStatementSegment"),
364 |         Ref("InsertStatementSegment"),
365 |         Ref("MergeStatementSegment"),  # New addition
366 |         # ... other statements
367 |     ),
368 | )
369 | ```
370 | 
371 | ### Adding Data Types
372 | 
373 | ```python
374 | tsql_dialect.replace(
375 |     DatatypeSegment=OneOf(
376 |         # Inherit ANSI types
377 |         Sequence("VARCHAR", Bracketed(Ref("NumericLiteralSegment"), optional=True)),
378 |         Sequence("INT"),
379 | 
380 |         # Add T-SQL specific types
381 |         Sequence("NVARCHAR",
382 |                  OneOf(Bracketed(Ref("NumericLiteralSegment")), "MAX", optional=True)),
383 |         Sequence("UNIQUEIDENTIFIER"),
384 |         Sequence("DATETIME2", Bracketed(Ref("NumericLiteralSegment"), optional=True)),
385 |         Sequence("HIERARCHYID"),
386 |     ),
387 | )
388 | ```
389 | 
390 | ## Testing Dialect Changes
391 | 
392 | ### Dialect-Specific Tests
393 | 
394 | Located in `test/dialects/<dialect>_test.py`:
395 | 
396 | ```python
397 | """Tests specific to T-SQL dialect."""
398 | import pytest
399 | from sqlfluff.core import Linter
400 | 
401 | @pytest.fixture
402 | def tsql_linter():
403 |     """Provide T-SQL linter for tests."""
404 |     return Linter(dialect="tsql")
405 | 
406 | def test_top_clause_parsing(tsql_linter):
407 |     """Test TOP clause in SELECT."""
408 |     sql = "SELECT TOP 10 * FROM users;"
409 |     parsed = tsql_linter.parse_string(sql)
410 |     assert parsed.tree is not None
411 |     # Find TOP clause in parse tree
412 |     top_clause = parsed.tree.find("top_clause")
413 |     assert top_clause is not None
414 | ```
415 | 
416 | ### Regression Prevention
417 | 
418 | Always run the full fixture generation to ensure your changes don't break other dialects:
419 | 
420 | ```bash
421 | # Test all dialects
422 | tox -e generate-fixture-yml
423 | 
424 | # Or specific ones that might be affected
425 | tox -e generate-fixture-yml -- -d ansi -d postgres -d mysql
426 | ```
427 | 
428 | ## Per-Dialect Agent Instructions
429 | 
430 | For complex dialects with vendor-specific quirks, SEE detailed instructions:
431 | 
432 | **T-SQL**: `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_instructions/tsql.md`
433 | 
434 | ---
435 | 
436 | **See also:**
437 | - Root `AGENTS.md` for general project overview
438 | - `src/sqlfluff/AGENTS.md` for Python coding standards
439 | - `test/AGENTS.md` for testing conventions
440 | - Individual `dialect_instructions/<dialect>.md` files for dialect-specific guidance

1 | # Rust Components - AI Assistant Instructions
2 | 
3 | This file provides guidance for SQLFluff's Rust components.
4 | 
5 | ## Overview
6 | 
7 | The `sqlfluffrs/` directory contains an **experimental Rust implementation** of performance-critical SQLFluff components. This is an ongoing effort to accelerate lexing and parsing operations while maintaining compatibility with the Python implementation.
8 | 
9 | ## Project Status
10 | 
11 | **Current state**: Opt-in beta, gated by config (`core.use_rust_parser = auto`).
12 | Shipped as the `sqlfluff[rs]` extra since 4.0; planned to become the default
13 | from 5.0.
14 | 
15 | **What's migrated:**
16 | - **Lexer** — done; Rust tokenizes and returns `RsToken`s that Python wraps.
17 | - **Parser** — core done for **all dialects**, but **hybrid**: Rust returns a
18 |   lightweight `MatchResult` (slices/classes/inserts); Python's
19 |   `MatchResult.apply()` still builds the `BaseSegment` AST. A parallel,
20 |   id-addressable Rust arena (`_rs_tree`, `RsTree`/`RsHandle`) is built and cached
21 |   as the substrate for Rust-side rules (read-only to Python today).
22 | - **Linting rules** — mostly Python; **three experimental rules are wired end
23 |   to end**. CP01, CP03 and CP04 detection lives in the `sqlfluffrs_rules` crate
24 |   (CP02 and CP05 remain Python-only), runs over the arena's public read API
25 |   (`sqlfluffrs_parser::Arena`), and is dispatched by the linter via
26 |   `BaseRule._eval_rust` when **`core.use_rust_rules`** is enabled (default
27 |   `False`; also requires the Rust parser's arena, else it falls back per-rule to
28 |   Python). Each is validated at parity with its stock Python rule. **Fixing is
29 |   still Python-side** — the Rust rule returns `(leaf_index, fixed_raw)` and the
30 |   linter anchors a `LintFix`; Rust-side (mutating) fixing waits on the arena
31 |   mutation milestone. See `sqlfluffrs_rules/`, `BaseRule._eval_rust`, and PRs
32 |   #7984 (CP01) and #8069 (CP03/CP04).
33 | 
34 | **Not a replacement**: the Rust components work alongside Python. When
35 | `sqlfluffrs` is unavailable, Python falls back transparently (auto mode).
36 | 
37 | ## Structure
38 | 
39 | This is a **Cargo workspace** with several member crates — not a single `src/`
40 | tree. The root crate (`sqlfluffrs`) is a thin PyO3 extension module that
41 | aggregates the others; the real work lives in the member crates.
42 | 
43 | ```
44 | sqlfluffrs/
45 | ├── Cargo.toml              # Workspace root + root crate (cdylib + rlib)
46 | ├── pyproject.toml          # Python packaging (maturin) for the extension
47 | ├── sqlfluffrs.pyi          # Python type stubs (Rs* names); + py.typed marker
48 | ├── src/                    # Root crate — aggregation only
49 | │   ├── lib.rs              #   Library root
50 | │   ├── python.rs           #   #[pymodule] — registers all PyO3 classes
51 | │   └── test_harness.rs     #   Fixture-comparison test helpers
52 | ├── tests/                  # Integration tests (YAML/fixture parity vs Python)
53 | ├── benches/                # Criterion benchmarks (parser_bench, …)
54 | │
55 | ├── sqlfluffrs_types/       # LEAF crate — core data types (no internal deps):
56 | │   └── src/                #   Token, PositionMarker, Slice, config/, templater/,
57 | │                           #   GrammarInst / GrammarTables (flattened grammar)
58 | ├── sqlfluffrs_dialects/    # Dialect grammars + lexers (GENERATED — see below)
59 | │   ├── build.rs            #   Reruns utils/rustify.py when Python dialects change
60 | │   └── src/                #   block_comment.rs + generated dialect/<name>/*
61 | ├── sqlfluffrs_lexer/       # Tokenization        (deps: types, dialects)
62 | ├── sqlfluffrs_parser/      # Largest crate — table-driven + recursive parser
63 | │   └── src/parser/         #   core.rs, frame.rs, cache.rs, table_driven/*
64 | ├── sqlfluffrs_python/      # PyO3 wrapper shims (PyToken, PyPositionMarker, …)
65 | └── sqlfluffrs_benchmarks/  # TPC-H / TPC-DS fixture helpers
66 | ```
67 | 
68 | **Internal dependency graph:**
69 | 
70 | ```
71 | types ← dialects ← lexer ← parser ← root crate (sqlfluffrs) & benchmarks
72 | sqlfluffrs_python depends only on types; lexer/parser pull it in under
73 | the `python` feature.
74 | ```
75 | 
76 | > **Generated code:** the `dialect/<name>/{mod,matcher,parser}.rs` files under
77 | > `sqlfluffrs_dialects/src/` are produced by `utils/rustify.py` from the Python
78 | > dialect definitions — **never hand-edit them**. See "Syncing with Python".
79 | 
80 | ## Rust Development Setup
81 | 
82 | ### Requirements
83 | 
84 | - **Rust**: Install via [rustup](https://rustup.rs/)
85 |   ```bash
86 |   curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
87 |   ```
88 | - **Cargo**: Comes with Rust installation
89 | - **Python development headers**: Required for PyO3 bindings
90 | 
91 | ### Building Rust Components
92 | 
93 | ```bash
94 | # Navigate to Rust directory
95 | cd sqlfluffrs
96 | 
97 | # Build Rust library
98 | cargo build
99 | 
100 | # Build release (optimized)
101 | cargo build --release
102 | 
103 | # Run Rust tests
104 | cargo test
105 | 
106 | # Run with output
107 | cargo test -- --nocapture
108 | 
109 | # Check code without building
110 | cargo check
111 | 
112 | # Format code
113 | cargo fmt
114 | 
115 | # Lint code
116 | cargo clippy
117 | ```
118 | 
119 | ### Python Integration
120 | 
121 | The Rust components are exposed to Python via **PyO3** and packaged with
122 | **maturin** (see `pyproject.toml`). The extension is built with the `python`
123 | feature enabled, which pulls in `pyo3` and the `*/python` features of the lexer
124 | and parser crates.
125 | 
126 | ```bash
127 | # Build + install the extension into the active venv (rebuilds on Rust changes)
128 | cd sqlfluffrs
129 | maturin develop            # debug
130 | maturin develop --release  # optimized — use this for benchmarking
131 | 
132 | # A plain pip install also works (invokes maturin under the hood):
133 | pip install -e ./sqlfluffrs/
134 | ```
135 | 
136 | > Building the extension triggers `sqlfluffrs_dialects/build.rs`, which runs
137 | > `utils/rustify.py` to (re)generate dialect sources. It needs Python able to
138 | > `import sqlfluff`, so build from an environment where the repo's `src/` is on
139 | > `PYTHONPATH` (the build script handles this for isolated build envs).
140 | 
141 | ## Rust Coding Standards
142 | 
143 | ### Style
144 | 
145 | - **Follow Rust conventions**: Use `rustfmt` for formatting
146 | - **Naming**:
147 |   - `snake_case` for functions, variables, modules
148 |   - `PascalCase` for types, structs, enums, traits
149 |   - `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants
150 | - **Idiomatic Rust**: Prefer iterators, pattern matching, and ownership patterns
151 | 
152 | ### Error Handling
153 | 
154 | **Prefer `Result` and `?` operator:**
155 | ```rust
156 | fn parse_token(input: &str) -> Result<Token, ParseError> {
157 |     let trimmed = input.trim();
158 |     if trimmed.is_empty() {
159 |         return Err(ParseError::EmptyInput);
160 |     }
161 |     Ok(Token::new(trimmed))
162 | }
163 | 
164 | fn process() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
165 |     let token = parse_token("  SELECT  ")?;  // Use ? operator
166 |     // ... use token
167 |     Ok(())
168 | }
169 | ```
170 | 
171 | **Avoid `unwrap()` and `expect()` in production code:**
172 | ```rust
173 | // ❌ Bad: Can panic
174 | let value = some_option.unwrap();
175 | 
176 | // ✅ Good: Handle None case
177 | let value = match some_option {
178 |     Some(v) => v,
179 |     None => return Err(Error::MissingValue),
180 | };
181 | 
182 | // ✅ Also good: Use ? with Option
183 | let value = some_option.ok_or(Error::MissingValue)?;
184 | ```
185 | 
186 | **Exception**: `unwrap()` and `expect()` are acceptable in tests.
187 | 
188 | ### Testing
189 | 
190 | ```rust
191 | #[cfg(test)]
192 | mod tests {
193 |     use super::*;
194 | 
195 |     #[test]
196 |     fn test_token_parsing() {
197 |         let result = parse_token("SELECT");
198 |         assert!(result.is_ok());
199 |         assert_eq!(result.unwrap().value, "SELECT");
200 |     }
201 | 
202 |     #[test]
203 |     fn test_empty_input_fails() {
204 |         let result = parse_token("");
205 |         assert!(result.is_err());
206 |     }
207 | }
208 | ```
209 | 
210 | Run tests:
211 | ```bash
212 | cargo test

217 | ## Python-Rust Interface (PyO3)
218 | 
219 | ### Exposing Rust to Python
220 | 
221 | The public API is **class-based**, not free functions. The `#[pyclass]` wrappers
222 | live in the `sqlfluffrs_python` crate and in each component crate's `python.rs`
223 | (e.g. `PyLexer`, `PyParser`); they are all registered in the root crate's
224 | `src/python.rs`. Note the module uses the modern PyO3 `Bound` API:
225 | 
226 | ```rust
227 | // src/python.rs (abridged)
228 | use pyo3::prelude::*;
229 | use sqlfluffrs_lexer::{PyLexer, PySQLLexError};
230 | use sqlfluffrs_parser::{PyMatchResult, PyNode, PyParser, RsParseError};
231 | use sqlfluffrs_python::token::{PyCaseFold, PyToken};
232 | 
233 | #[pymodule(name = "sqlfluffrs", module = "sqlfluffrs")]
234 | fn sqlfluffrs(m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
235 |     m.add_class::<PyToken>()?;
236 |     m.add_class::<PyLexer>()?;
237 |     m.add_class::<PyParser>()?;
238 |     m.add_class::<PyNode>()?;
239 |     m.add_class::<PyMatchResult>()?;
240 |     m.add("RsParseError", m.py().get_type::<RsParseError>())?;
241 |     Ok(())
242 | }
243 | ```
244 | 
245 | These classes are surfaced to Python under their `Rs*` aliases (e.g. `PyLexer`
246 | → `RsLexer`, `PyParser` → `RsParser`); the Python side imports them in
247 | `src/sqlfluff/core/parser/{lexer.py,rust_parser.py}` behind a try/except so a
248 | missing extension degrades to pure Python.
249 | 
250 | ### Type Stubs
251 | 
252 | Public types are declared in `sqlfluffrs.pyi` under their `Rs*` names, e.g.:
253 | 
254 | ```python
255 | class RsLexer:
256 |     def _lex(self, lex_input: object) -> object: ...
257 | 
258 | class RsParser:
259 |     def parse_match_result_from_tokens(self, ...) -> RsMatchResult: ...
260 | ```
261 | 
262 | ## Architecture
263 | 
264 | The pipeline is **lex → parse**, with dialect grammars supplied as flat tables.
265 | 
266 | ### Lexer (`sqlfluffrs_lexer`)
267 | 
268 | `Lexer` (in `sqlfluffrs_lexer/src/lexer.rs`) turns a SQL string (plus templater
269 | metadata) into a `Vec<Token>` using the dialect's `LexMatcher`s. Tokens and
270 | `PositionMarker`s are defined in `sqlfluffrs_types`.
271 | 
272 | ### Grammar representation (`sqlfluffrs_types`)
273 | 
274 | Python's grammar AST (`Sequence`, `OneOf`, `Bracketed`, `Delimited`, `Ref`,
275 | `StringParser`, …) is **not** modelled as a tree of trait objects. Instead it is
276 | **flattened by codegen** into compact static tables — `GrammarInst` (~20 bytes
277 | each) indexed by `GrammarId`, plus side tables (`CHILD_IDS`, `TERMINATORS`,
278 | `STRINGS`, `AUX_DATA`, `SIMPLE_HINTS`, …). See `grammar_inst.rs` /
279 | `grammar_tables.rs`. This keeps a dialect ~1 MB instead of tens of MB of boxed
280 | nodes and avoids per-node heap allocation.
281 | 
282 | ### Parser (`sqlfluffrs_parser`)
283 | 
284 | A **table-driven** engine walks those tables. The hot path is the iterative,
285 | frame-based executor in `src/parser/table_driven/` (one module per grammar
286 | variant: `sequence.rs`, `oneof.rs`, `bracketed.rs`, `delimited.rs`,
287 | `anynumberof.rs`, `ref_grammar.rs`, plus `iterative.rs` driving the frame stack).
288 | `oneof.rs` uses pre-computed `SimpleHint`s to prune alternatives cheaply. The
289 | parser produces a `MatchResult`, not a finished AST (Python builds the AST — see
290 | Project Status).
291 | 
292 | ### Dialect support (`sqlfluffrs_dialects`)
293 | 
294 | All Python dialects are mirrored here as **generated** modules. Each dialect gets
295 | `matcher.rs` (lexers + keyword sets) and `parser.rs` (the grammar tables above),
296 | dispatched through a generated `Dialect` enum. Do not edit by hand — regenerate
297 | via `utils/rustify.py` (see "Syncing with Python").
298 | 
299 | ## Performance Considerations
300 | 
301 | ### Benchmarking
302 | 
303 | Use Criterion for benchmarks:
304 | 
305 | ```rust
306 | // benches/lexer_bench.rs
307 | use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion};
308 | 
309 | fn lexer_benchmark(c: &mut Criterion) {
310 |     c.bench_function("lex_simple_select", |b| {
311 |         b.iter(|| {
312 |             let sql = black_box("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1");
313 |             lex(sql)
314 |         });
315 |     });
316 | }
317 | 
318 | criterion_group!(benches, lexer_benchmark);
319 | criterion_main!(benches);
320 | ```
321 | 
322 | Run benchmarks:
323 | ```bash
324 | cargo bench
325 | ```
326 | 
327 | Criterion measures the Rust internals in isolation. To see how the cost is
328 | split across the **Python↔Rust boundary** when SQLFluff actually drives the
329 | Rust parser, use the per-stage profiler instead (see below).
330 | 
331 | ### Profiling the Python↔Rust parse path
332 | 
333 | `RustParser.parse()` (in `src/sqlfluff/core/parser/rust_parser.py`) is a fast
334 | Rust core wrapped in O(nodes) Python work. The profiler splits a parse into
335 | four stages so you can see where the time goes:
336 | 
337 | - `rust_core` — the Rust parse (`parse_match_result_from_tokens`)
338 | - `convert` — rebuilding the result as a Python `MatchResult`
339 | - `apply` — building the `BaseSegment` tree (`MatchResult.apply`)
340 | - `apply_as_tree` — building the Rust arena tree (`_rs_tree`)
341 | 
342 | Enable it via the `SQLFLUFF_RS_PROFILE` env var or `set_profiling(True)`, then
343 | read the most recent parse with `get_parse_profile()`. The benchmark harness
344 | surfaces it directly (overall + small/medium/large file buckets):
345 | 
346 | ```bash
347 | # Requires the Rust parser (--compare or --rust-only); no effect on pure Python.
348 | python utils/benchmark_parsing.py --dialect ansi --rust-only --profile
349 | ```
350 | 
351 | As a rule of thumb, the Python-side stages dominate parse time on small/medium
352 | files (the FFI/tree-build overhead is not yet amortised), while `rust_core`
353 | dominates on large files.
354 | 
355 | ### Optimization
356 | 
357 | - Use `cargo build --release` for production builds
358 | - Profile with `cargo flamegraph` or `perf`
359 | - Prefer zero-copy operations where possible
360 | - Use `&str` over `String` when ownership not needed

362 | ## Development Workflow
363 | 
364 | ### Making Changes
365 | 
366 | 1. **Edit Rust code** in the relevant member crate (e.g. `sqlfluffrs_parser/src/`)
367 | 2. **Run tests:**
368 |    ```bash
369 |    cargo test                 # workspace-wide
370 |    cargo test -p sqlfluffrs_parser   # a single crate
371 |    ```
372 | 3. **Format code:**
373 |    ```bash
374 |    cargo fmt
375 |    ```
376 | 4. **Lint:**
377 |    ```bash
378 |    cargo clippy
379 |    ```
380 | 5. **Build Python extension:**
381 |    ```bash
382 |    maturin develop --release
383 |    ```
384 | 6. **Test Python integration:**
385 |    ```python
386 |    import sqlfluffrs
387 |    # exercise RsLexer / RsParser from Python
388 |    ```
389 | 
390 | ### Syncing with Python
391 | 
392 | The dialect grammars/lexers are **generated from the Python dialect
393 | definitions** in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/`. After changing a Python dialect (or
394 | the generators in `utils/build_*.py`):
395 | 
396 | 1. **Regenerate the Rust dialect sources:**
397 |    ```bash
398 |    # From repository root, in an env where `import sqlfluff` works
399 |    source venv/bin/activate
400 |    python utils/rustify.py build      # `check` verifies output is up to date (CI)
401 |    ```
402 |    (A normal `cargo build` / `maturin develop` also triggers this via
403 |    `sqlfluffrs_dialects/build.rs` when Python sources are newer.)
404 | 
405 | 2. **Confirm parity against the Python suite:**
406 |    ```bash
407 |    tox -e py312
408 |    ```
409 |    Cross-language parity is also checked by the Rust integration tests in
410 |    `tests/` (e.g. `fixture_tests.rs`), which compare Rust parse output against
411 |    the YAML fixtures used by the Python tests.

413 | ## Common Tasks
414 | 
415 | ### Adjusting Lexing Behaviour
416 | 
417 | 1. Edit the lexer engine in `sqlfluffrs_lexer/src/lexer.rs`.
418 | 2. Note: the per-dialect lexer matchers/keywords are **generated** into
419 |    `sqlfluffrs_dialects/src/dialect/<name>/matcher.rs` — to change *those*,
420 |    edit the Python dialect and regenerate (next section), don't hand-edit.
421 | 3. Write tests, run `cargo test`.
422 | 
423 | ### Updating a Dialect
424 | 
425 | Dialect grammars are generated, so the source of truth is **Python**:
426 | 
427 | 1. Edit `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_<name>.py` (keywords, grammar, etc.).
428 | 2. Regenerate: `python utils/rustify.py build`.
429 | 3. Test parity: `cargo test` (fixtures) and `tox -e py312-rust`.
430 | 
431 | ### Exposing a New Class to Python
432 | 
433 | 1. Add a `#[pyclass]` in `sqlfluffrs_python` (or the owning component crate's
434 |    `python.rs`).
435 | 2. Register it in the root crate's `src/python.rs`:
436 |    ```rust
437 |    m.add_class::<PyMyThing>()?;
438 |    ```
439 | 3. Add the corresponding `Rs*` type to `sqlfluffrs.pyi`.
440 | 4. Wire it into the Python side (`src/sqlfluff/core/parser/…`) behind the
441 |    existing try/except import so a missing extension still degrades gracefully.
442 | 5. Rebuild with `maturin develop` and test.

481 | ## Current Limitations
482 | 
483 | - **Linting is mostly Python** — only the CP01/CP03/CP04 detection loops run
484 |   in Rust, behind `core.use_rust_rules` (default off). Every other rule, and the
485 |   whole fix/format pipeline, is still Python; the arena (`_rs_tree`) is
486 |   read-only, so Rust-side fixing waits on the arena mutation milestone.
487 | - **Hybrid parse** — Rust returns a `MatchResult`; Python still builds the AST.
488 | - **Performance gains scale with file size** — small files see little benefit
489 |   because of the Python↔Rust crossing overhead.
490 | - All shipped dialects are mirrored and parity-tested against the Python
491 |   fixtures, so dialect *coverage* is not a current limitation.
